description: Greenheart is a very dense, strong, and rot-resistant timber from the Guiana Shield. It is used for marine and dock work, lock gates, heavy construction, factory flooring, and traditionally for fishing rods and tool handles.

hazards.summary: The UK HSE lists greenheart among woods whose splinters tend to heal slowly and often become infected.
The UK HSE reports heart-related disorders among the adverse health effects associated with greenheart.
The UK HSE also lists intestinal (gut) disorders among the reported effects of working with greenheart.
Severe throat irritation from greenheart dust is listed by the UK HSE.
All wood dust, including greenheart, is classified by IARC as carcinogenic to humans, mainly linked to cancers of the nose and sinuses after long-term exposure.

image_prompt: Photorealistic studio photograph of a freshly planed greenheart (Chlorocardium rodiei) board, shot at a low three-quarter angle so the face grain fills most of the frame. Yellowish olive-green to medium olive-brown heartwood with a few darker brown streaks, grading into slightly paler yellow-green sapwood along one edge without a sharp boundary. Fine, very even texture with straight to slightly interlocked grain, small evenly scattered pores, and a medium natural luster. Soft diffused daylight from upper left, gentle falloff, neutral warm-grey seamless background, shallow depth of field with the near edge tack-sharp. No text, no logos, no hands, no tools, no finish or varnish, natural unfinished wood. Wide 1200x630 composition (1.91:1) with the board centered and margin on both sides for cropping.
image_alt: Planed board of greenheart with olive-green to olive-brown heartwood, a few darker streaks, and a fine even texture.
notes_internal: All greenheart hazards rest on HSE-WIS30 Table 2 only (read from a third-party-hosted copy of WIS30 rev 1; the hse.gov.uk/pubns/wis30.pdf URL returned an HTML page, so the live URL still needs confirming). WIS30 gives no route or mechanism for cardiac/intestinal effects; route set to inhalation as an assumption - review. No PubMed primary reports found for greenheart health effects. WIS30 does not give a botanical name; mapping to Chlorocardium rodiei is standard trade usage, name checked on GBIF only. WIS30 copy carries an Open Government Licence footer. No reports for a given effect does not mean the wood is safe.
